mcq: Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is referred to as accelerated erosion."
Erosion occurring under this condition is referred to as accelerated erosion.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ refers to the degree to which soil particles are clumped together, forming larger clumps and pore spaces."
Structure refers to the degree to which soil particles are clumped together, forming larger clumps and pore spaces.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is the redistribution of soil through the action of tillage and gravity."
Tillage erosion Tillage erosion is the redistribution of soil through the action of tillage and gravity.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is a type of no-tillage system which is used in the dryland areas in the USA."
No-till fallow is a type of no-tillage system which is used in the dryland areas in the USA.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is a very complicated problem as many complex factors affect the rate of erosion and therefore it is difficult to solve."
Soil erosion is a very complicated problem as many complex factors affect the rate of erosion and therefore it is difficult to solve.

Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is a specialized type of conservation tillage consisting of a one-pass planting and fertilizer operation in which the soil and the surface residues are minimally disturbed."

No-tillage The no-till system is a specialized type of conservation tillage consisting of a one-pass planting and fertilizer operation in which the soil and the surface residues are minimally disturbed.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is the movement of soil from raindrop splash and runoff water."
Sheet erosion Sheet erosion is the movement of soil from raindrop splash and runoff water.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is composed of mineral and organic matter and is capable of sustaining plant life."
The soil layer is composed of mineral and organic matter and is capable of sustaining plant life.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is defined as the soil-related actions necessary for crop production (Boone 1988)."
Tillage is defined as the soil-related actions necessary for crop production (Boone 1988).
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ refers to the size or combination of sizes of the individual soil particles."
Texture refers to the size or combination of sizes of the individual soil particles.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is a two (2)-credit unit course on Soil and Water Management."
SLM308 is a two (2)-credit unit course on Soil and Water Management.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is the entrainment and movement of detached soil particles (sediment) from their original location."
Transportation is the entrainment and movement of detached soil particles (sediment) from their original location.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is the inherent yielding or nonresistance of soils and rocks to erosion."
Erodability (or erodibility) is the inherent yielding or nonresistance of soils and rocks to erosion.
fib: ______ is the natural cover of soil.
Vegetation
Vegetation is the natural cover of soil.
______ is used in nearly every aspect of life.
Water
Water is used in nearly every aspect of life.
______ is used in mechanised wheat farming in northern Tanzania and for some perennial crops, for example coffee plantations.
No-tillage
No-tillage is used in mechanised wheat farming in northern Tanzania and for some perennial crops, for example coffee plantations.
______ is an advanced stage of rill erosion where surface channels are eroded to the point where they become a nuisance factor in normal tillage operations.
Gully erosion
Gully erosion Gully erosion is an advanced stage of rill erosion where surface channels are eroded to the point where they become a nuisance factor in normal tillage operations.
______ is the prevention of soil loss from erosion or reduced fertility caused by over usage, acidification, salinization or other chemical soil contamination.
Soil conservation technique
Soil conservation technique is the prevention of soil loss from erosion or reduced fertility caused by over usage, acidification, salinization or other chemical soil contamination.
______ is responsible for this erosion although in many locations wind, glaciers are also the agents causing soil erosion.
Mainly water
Mainly water is responsible for this erosion although in many locations wind, glaciers are also the agents causing soil erosion.
______ is defined as the control of soil erosion in order to maintain agricultural productivity.
Soil conservation
Soil conservation is defined as the control of soil erosion in order to maintain agricultural productivity.
______ is the term used to describe the potential of raindrop impact, runoff from snowmelt, or water applied with an irrigation system rainstorm to detach and erode soil.
Erosivity
Erosivity is the term used to describe the potential of raindrop impact, runoff from snowmelt, or water applied with an irrigation system rainstorm to detach and erode soil.
______ is the progressive undercutting, scouring and slumping of these drainage ways.
Bank erosion
Bank erosion is the progressive undercutting, scouring and slumping of these drainage ways.

______ is a rich natural fertilizer and soil conditioner that aerates soil, improves its ability to retain water and nutrients, helps prevent erosion and prevents nutrients from being wasted in landfills.
Compost

Compost is a rich natural fertilizer and soil conditioner that aerates soil, improves its ability to retain water and nutrients, helps prevent erosion and prevents nutrients from being wasted in landfills.
______ are those activities at the local level which maintain or enhance the productive capacity of the land including soil, water and vegetation in areas prone to degradation through.
Soil and water conservation techniques

Soil and water conservation techniques are those activities at the local level which maintain or enhance the productive capacity of the land including soil, water and vegetation in areas prone to degradation through.
______ are the basis for sustainable farming systems that incorporate integrated nutrient management.
Nitrogen-fixing legumes
Nitrogen-fixing legumes are the basis for sustainable farming systems that incorporate integrated nutrient management.
______ is a key to conserving water.
Proper soil management
Proper soil management Proper soil management is a key to conserving water.
